text:
maria: quick heads-up — during last night's load run we saw a weird tail-latency bump on the dedicated pool when short-seq traffic jumped. not catastrophic but reproducible :thinking_face:
jon: saw it too. timeline? pct of long vs short at the spike?
maria: around 22:17 UTC, short sequences (<=16 tokens) rose from 18% -> 46%. 10 minute window. median stable, p95 moved from 52ms -> 110ms.
praveen: can you paste profiler dump? I'm curious if the runtime switched kernels or batch size distribution changed.
maria: attaching quick snippet from the runtime trace:```
KER: attention_fwd         49.2%
KER: gelu_fast             18.7%
KER: kv_lookup_apply       12.9%
KER: tokenizer_postproc    7.1%
MED_LAT_MS: 56
P95_LAT_MS: 112
BATCH_SZ_DIST: [1:34%, 2-4:41%, 5+:25%]
```
anya: that batch size shift looks like batching window collapsed — lots of small singletons. Could be our batch formation threshold reacting to short bursts.
jon: does the kernel selection log show fastpath->fallback churn? that would explain the step-up.
praveen: checked earlier: when batch token budget drops below 48 tokens we hit a different attention kernel that is ~1.8x slower on Ampere. Kernel swap log: `attention_selected=attn_v2_fast || attn_v1_fallback` and fallback rate increased 3x during spike.
kai: why would token budget drop? maybe queue policy refilled credits slower because long sequences were occupying token reservoirs?
maria: possible. we did a recent change to token refill window (refill_ms from 200 -> 350) to stabilize cost. suspect that change reduced effective short-seq admit rate during bursts.
jon: interesting. so tradeoff between cost smoothing and short-request fairness. we need a rule that reserves a tiny fastpath budget for short sequences so they don't force kernel fallback.
praveen: experiment proposal: add a per-tenant short-reserve capacitor = min(8 tokens or 10% of tenant budget) that is refilled faster (100ms). This keeps small sequences coalesced into the fastpath kernel.
anya: +1. also we should prefer coalescing short requests into the next micro-batch for up to 12ms instead of immediately dispatching singletons. Implement with jittered micro-wait to avoid herd.
kai: quick sims? I can run the batcher simulator with current distribution and proposed reserve.
jon: please also profile KV priming: if KV cache warmup is slow when short bursts happen, long sequences might be penalized too. we need to track KV hit-rate by sequence length.
praveen: ran a small sim locally: with short-reserve enabled p95 drops ~35% in the short-burst scenario and kernel fallback rate goes back to baseline. cost delta ~+0.6% for that window.
maria: that's promising. what about multi-tenant fairness when one tenant spikes short seqs while others have long requests?
praveen: plan: enforce reserve per tenant with a global cap so a noisy neighbor can't consume all fastpath reserves. Reservoir algorithm: tenant_reserve = clamp(min(8, 0.1*tenant_tokens), 0, global_fast_cap_per_shard).
anya: and add telemetry: emit `fast_reserve_used`, `fallback_rate_by_kernel`, `kv_hit_by_len_bucket`, and `batch_coalesce_delay_hist` so we can TTI the change.
kai: I've queued a simulator run across 500 tenant mixes; will post numbers in ~20m. `ci-batcher-sim --mix config/500-mixes.yaml --short-reserve 8 --refill-ms 100`
buildbot: CI note: batcher unit tests + integration smoke passed on linux-amd64. regression test `batch_coalesce_delay` added.
jon: next steps: 1) kai posts sims 2) praveen drafts patch for short-reserve + refill tuning 3) anya adds telemetry + dashboard panel 4) maria runs a canary on a single dedicated shard with mixed tenants.
maria: ok doing the canary tomorrow 02:00 UTC. will monitor `fallback_rate_by_kernel` and `p95_by_len_bucket`. ping me if we need to roll back. :rocket:
praveen: I'll include a quick rollback knob `--short-reserve=0` and a guardian rule that disables reserve if global load > 95% GPU util.
anya: good call. also add alert for reserve causing increased queuing beyond 30ms for long sequences.
jon: thanks all. this feels less like a starvation bug and more like tuning drift from the refill change. still glad we have a small mitigation that keeps the fastpath healthy.
kai: sims finished: in synthetic mix where short spikes to 50%: p95 short down 38%, long p95 up 4% but median unchanged. global cost +0.9% in tight windows. uploading csv to #eng-runtime in 3m.
maria: perfect. we'll iterate after canary. thanks everyone.
buildbot: deploy note: canary image built: gcr.io/redwood-inference/batcher:canary-short-reserve-20260712, scheduled to shard-id 7 at 02:00 UTC.
